One other violin of similar size by Antonio Stradivari is known to exist. This is the "Aiglon" violin, ascribed to the date 1734. Preserved in the Ala Ponzone Civic Museum in Cremona is Stradivari's original mould which he used for the constuction of such small-sized instruments. Also in the Museum are paper patterns for the side elevation and the shield finials used on both the "Aiglon" and the present violin. See Simone F. Sacconi, The Secrets of Stradivari, Page 34, Figures 30, 31 and 32, Catalogue Number 54 (See Colour Plate)
